program.tagline: THE FUTURE, ONE BYTE AT A TIME

segments.text: Chipmaker unveils a laptop processor with all-day battery life. Also coming up: rocket launches a probe to study the Sun's poles. And later, our number of the day. This is TECH BYTES. I'm Max Circuit, with Ada Volt.
The first laptops using it will go on sale in the spring, Circuit Weekly reports. A chipmaker has unveiled a new laptop processor it says can run for 20 hours on a single charge.
segments.headline: Chipmaker unveils laptop processor with all-day battery life

segments.text: Thanks, Max. A rocket has launched a probe that will study the Sun's poles for the first time. The journey to its final orbit will take 3 years, according to Starfield Journal.
segments.headline: Rocket launches probe to study Sun's poles

segments.text: Our number of the day: 50,000. A research ship has mapped 50,000 square kilometres of sea floor near Antarctica. The maps reveal underwater canyons and an extinct volcano, Starfield Journal reports.
segments.headline: Scientists map ocean floor near Antarctica in new detail

segments.text: And finally: A home robotics company has shown a robot vacuum that can climb stairs using two small legs. It will cost about 1,500 dollars when it launches next year, according to Circuit Weekly.
segments.headline: Robot vacuum learns to climb stairs

segments.text: The engineer in me approves. The accountant in me is less sure.
That's TECH BYTES. From Ada Volt and from me, thanks for watching. More news around the clock on GLOBIT 24.

rundown.headline: Chipmaker unveils laptop processor with all-day battery life
Rocket launches probe to study Sun's poles
Scientists map ocean floor near Antarctica in new detail
Robot vacuum learns to climb stairs
